paper.title: Multi-channel Autobidding with Budget and ROI Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Optimizing per-channel budgets under bandit feedback (single-item auctions), cumulative loss vs GL-OPT
unmapped: Decision is a vector of M per-channel budgets in [0,rho]^M; per-channel conversion V_j(rho_j) is concave, piecewise linear, increasing (reward is concave, i.e. loss convex)

Unknown (uncertain) ROI constraint sum_j E[V_j(rho_j)] >= gamma * sum_j rho_j and budget constraint sum_j rho_j <= rho, holding in expectation; learner observes realized conversion and spend per channel (one-point feedback)
Value-cost pairs drawn i.i.d. from a finite-support discrete distribution per channel; channels optimally solve an LP knapsack autobidding problem
The learner knows the global target ROI gamma and total budget rho
settings.definition_quote: at the beginning of period $t\in [T]$, the advertiser sets per-channel budgets $(\rho_{j,t})_{j\in [M]}$, while simultaneously values and costs ... are sampled (independently in each period) from finite support $F$ ... the advertiser only observes the numerical values $\totv_{j}(\rho_{j,t}; \bm{z}_{j,t})$ and $\totc_{j}(\rho_{j,t}; \bm{z}_{j,t})$

settings.name_in_paper: Optimizing per-channel budgets under bandit feedback (single-item auctions), accuracy of output budget profile
unmapped: Decision is a vector of M per-channel budgets in [0,rho]^M; per-channel conversion V_j(rho_j) is concave, piecewise linear, increasing
Unknown ROI and budget constraints in expectation; output must satisfy them in expectation; one-point bandit feedback of realized conversion and spend
Value-cost pairs drawn i.i.d. from finite-support discrete distributions; channels optimally autobid
The learner knows the global target ROI gamma and total budget rho
settings.definition_quote: At the end of $T$ periods, the algorithm produces some per-channel budget profile $(\rho_{j})_{j\in [M]}\in [0,\rho]^{M}$ that approximates $\textsc{CH-OPT}(\mathcal{I}_{\budg})$, and satisfies aggregate ROI and budget constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Per-channel budget optimization for multi-item auctions with increasing marginal values, accuracy of output
unmapped: Each auction sells multiple impressions, at most one procured per auction; auctions have increasing marginal values (e.g. VCG)
Unknown ROI and budget constraints in expectation; one-point bandit feedback
The learner knows the global target ROI gamma and total budget rho
settings.definition_quote: For each auction $n\in [m_{j}]$ of channel $j\in [M]$, assume $L_{j,n} \in \N$ impressions are sold, and channel $j$ is only allowed to procure at most 1 impression in auction $n$ on the advertiser's behalf.

conditions: Assumption 4.1 (moderate budgets: channel solutions are budget binding, rho < infinity)
Assumption 4.2 (strictly feasible ROI constraint in every channel realization)
value-cost pairs from finite-support discrete distributions with strict ordering of value-to-cost ratios
conversion bounded by known constant Vbar

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Assume assumptions \ref{ass:budgetbind} and \ref{ass:feas} hold. Take step size $\eta = \Theta(1/\sqrt{T})$, discretization width $\discerr = \Theta(T^{-1/3}) $ and $\safe = \safebudg = \frac{1}{\log(T)}$ in Algorithm \ref{alg:omducb}, as well as $\underline{\slope} = \Theta(T^{-1/3})$ in Lemma \ref{lem:ucbregret}. Then, for large enough $T$ we have $ T\cdot \textsc{GL-OPT} - \E\left[\sum_{t\in [T]}\sum_{j\in[M]}\totv_{j}(\rho_{j,t})\right] \leq \mathcal{O}(T^{2/3})$.

results.notes: Regret is measured against T times the optimal constrained value GL-OPT using expected conversion functions, so pseudo-regret type. Hidden constants depend on the instance (support F, distribution p, M, rho, gamma, Vbar); the proof's lemmas hide log factors (Õ), though the theorem states O.

conditions: finite-support value-cost distributions with strict ordering of value-to-cost ratios
conversion bounded by known constant Vbar

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Further, recalling $\overline{\bm{\rho}}_{T}$ is the final output of Algorithm \ref{alg:omducb}, we have \textsc{GL-OPT} - \sum_{j \in [M]}\E\left[\totv_{j}(\overline{\rho}_{j,T})\right] \leq \mathcal{O}(T^{-1/3}) and constraint satisfaction: $\rho - \sum_{j \in [M]}\E[\overline{\rho}_{j,T}]\geq 0$, as well as $\sum_{j \in [M]} \E[\totv_{j}(\overline{\rho}_{j,T}) -\gamma\overline{\rho}_{j,T}] \geq 0 $.

results.notes: Accuracy of the averaged output budget profile; also guarantees ROI and budget constraint satisfaction in expectation. Quantity mapped to simple_regret (gap of recommended point).

conditions: all multi-item auctions have increasing marginal values (Definition 5.1)
Assumptions 4.1 and 4.2 hold for the multi-item setting

source.quote: Assume multi-item auctions in any channel $j\in [M]$ has increasing marginal values (per Definition \ref{def:incrmarginal}), and assume Assumptions \ref{ass:budgetbind} and \ref{ass:feas} hold for the multi-item setting. Then with the same parameter choices as in Theorem \ref{thm:regret}, ... we have \textsc{GL-OPT}^{+} - \sum_{j \in [M]}\E\left[\totv_{j}^{+}(\overline{\rho}_{T,j})\right] \leq \mathcal{O}(T^{-1/3})\,, as well as constraint satisfaction

results.notes: Proof omitted in paper (identical to Theorem 4.6). Also guarantees constraint satisfaction in expectation.
